section.heading: Short Title and commencement

content.p: This Act may be cited as the Copyright Act 1994.
Except as provided in sections 27(2) and 144(5), this Act shall come into force on 1 January 1995.

section.heading: Interpretation

content.p: In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires,—
References in this Act to the time at which a literary, dramatic, or musical work is made are to the time at which the work is recorded, in writing or otherwise.

section.heading: Associated definitions for communication works

blockList.listIntroduction: References in this Act to a person making a communication work are—

item.p: to the person transmitting the communication work or making it available by means of a communication technology, if that person has responsibility to any extent for its contents; and
any person who provides the contents of the work and who makes with the person communicating the work the arrangements necessary for its communication.

blockList.listIntroduction: For the purposes of this Act, in the case of communicating a work by satellite transmission,—

item.p: the place from which the work is communicated is the place from which the signals carrying the work are transmitted to the satellite; and
the person communicating the work is the person who transmits those signals to the satellite.

section.heading: Meaning of cable programme service, and associated definitions
Meaning of author

content.p: For the purposes of this Act, the author of a work is the person who creates it.

blockList.listIntroduction: For the purposes of subsection (1), the person who creates a work shall be taken to be,—

item.p: in the case of a literary, dramatic, musical, or artistic work that is computer-generated, the person by whom the arrangements necessary for the creation of the work are undertaken:
in the case of a sound recording or film, the person by whom the arrangements necessary for the making of the recording or film are undertaken:
in the case of a communication work, the person who makes the communication work:
in the case of a typographical arrangement of a published edition, the publisher.

content.p: The author of a work of any of the descriptions referred to in subsection (2) may be a natural person or a body corporate.

section.heading: Meaning of work of joint authorship

content.p: In this Act, the term work of joint authorship means a work produced by the collaboration of 2 or more authors in which the contribution of each author is not distinct from that of the other author or authors.
A communication work must be treated as a work of joint authorship in any case where more than 1 person is to be taken as making the communication work.
References in this Act to the author of a work shall be construed in relation to a work of joint authorship as a reference to all the authors of the work.

Where, in relation to a work of joint authorship, copyright would not exist in the work if 1 or more of the authors were the sole author or sole joint authors, the work shall be treated as if the other author or authors were the sole author or sole joint authors of the work.

section.heading: Meaning of unknown authorship

content.p: For the purposes of this Act, a work is of unknown authorship if the identity of the author is unknown or, in the case of a work of joint authorship, if the identity of none of the authors is known.

For the purposes of this Act, the identity of an author shall be regarded as unknown if it is not possible for a person who wishes to ascertain the identity of the author to do so by reasonable inquiry; but if that identity is once known it shall not subsequently be regarded as unknown.

section.heading: Meaning of copyright owner

content.p: Where copyright or any aspect of copyright is owned by more than 1 person jointly, references in this Act to the copyright owner, or to the owner of the copyright in the work, are to all owners.

Where different persons are entitled to different aspects of copyright in a work, the copyright owner for any purpose of this Act is the person who is entitled to the aspect of copyright relevant for that purpose.

Subject to the provisions of Part 7, where a question arises under this Act whether an object of any description has been imported, sold, or otherwise dealt with other than pursuant to a copyright licence, the copyright owner shall be taken to be the person entitled to the copyright in respect of its application to the making of objects of that description in the country into which the object was imported or in which it was sold or otherwise dealt with.

section.heading: Meaning of issue to the public

blockList.listIntroduction: References in this Act to the issue of copies of a work to the public mean the act of putting into circulation copies not previously put into circulation; and do not include the acts of—

item.p: subsequent distribution or sale of those copies; or
subject to subsections (2) and (3), subsequent hiring or loan of those copies; or
subsequent importation of those copies into New Zealand; or
distribution of imported copies that are not infringing copies within the meaning of section 12 subsequent to their importation into New Zealand.

blockList.listIntroduction: The issue of copies of a work to the public, in relation to computer programs, includes the rental of copies of computer programs to the public and rental subsequent to those works having been put into circulation; but does not include any such rental where—

item.p: the computer program is incorporated into any other thing; and
the rental of the computer program is not the principal purpose or one of the principal purposes of the rental; and
the computer program cannot readily be copied by the hirer.

content.p: The issue of copies of a work to the public, in relation to sound recordings and films, includes the rental of copies of those works to the public and rental subsequent to those works having been put into circulation.

section.heading: Meaning of publication

blockList.listIntroduction: In this Act, the term publication, in relation to a work,—

item.p: means the issue of copies of the work to the public; and
includes, in the case of a literary, dramatic, musical, or artistic work, making it available to the public by means of an electronic retrieval system;—

content.p: and publish has a corresponding meaning.

In the case of a work of architecture in the form of a building, or an artistic work incorporated in a building, construction of the building shall be treated as equivalent to publication of the work.
References in this Act to publication do not include publication that is not intended to satisfy the reasonable requirements of the public.

blockList.listIntroduction: The following acts do not constitute publication for the purposes of this Act:

item.p: in the case of a literary, dramatic, or musical work,—
the performance of the work; or
the communication of the work to the public (otherwise than for the purposes of an electronic retrieval system):
in the case of any artistic work,—
the exhibition of the work; or
the issue to the public of copies of a film including the work; or
the communication of the work to the public (otherwise than for the purposes of an electronic retrieval system):
in the case of an artistic work being— the issue to the public of copies of a graphic work representing, or of photographs of, the work:
a sculpture; or
a work of architecture in the form of a building or a model for a building; or
a work of artistic craftsmanship,—
in the case of a sound recording or film,—
the playing or showing of the work in public; or
the communication of the work to the public.

content.p: No account shall be taken for the purposes of this section of any unauthorised act.

section.heading: Meaning of commercial publication

blockList.listIntroduction: In this Act, the term commercial publication, in relation to a literary, dramatic, musical, or artistic work, means the publication of the work consisting of—

item.p: issuing copies of the work to the public at a time when copies made in advance of the receipt of orders are generally available to the public; or
making the work available to the public by means of an electronic retrieval system;—

content.p: and related expressions shall be construed accordingly.

section.heading: Meaning of infringing copy

content.p: In this Act, the term infringing copy, in relation to a copyright work, shall be construed in accordance with this section.
An object is an infringing copy if its making constitutes an infringement of the copyright in the work in question.

blockList.listIntroduction: An object that a person imports, or proposes to import, into New Zealand is an infringing copy if—

item.p: the making of the object constituted an infringement of the copyright in the work in question in the country in which the object was made; or

the importer would have infringed the copyright in the work in question in New Zealand had the importer made the object in New Zealand, unless the object is one to which subsection (5A) or subsection (6) applies.

blockList.listIntroduction: Where in any proceedings the question arises whether an object is an infringing copy, and it is shown—

item.p: that the object is a copy of the work in question; and
that copyright exists in the work or has existed at any time,—

content.p: it shall be presumed until the contrary is proved that the object was made at a time when copyright existed in the work.

blockList.listIntroduction: In this Act, an infringing copy includes a copy falling to be treated as an infringing copy under any of the following provisions of this Act:

item.p: section 85(4) (which relates to incidental recording for the purposes of a communication work):
section 93(1) (which relates to subsequent dealings with copies made under Part 3).

blockList.listIntroduction: An object that a person imports or proposes to import into New Zealand is not an infringing copy under subsection (3)﻿(b) if—

item.p: it was made by or with the consent of the owner of the copyright, or other equivalent intellectual property right, in the work in question in the country in which the object was made; or
where no person owned the copyright, or other equivalent intellectual property right, in the work in question in the country in which the object was made, any of the following applies:
the copyright protection (or other equivalent intellectual property right protection) formerly afforded to the work in question in that country has expired:

the person otherwise entitled to be the owner of the copyright (or other equivalent intellectual property right) in the work in question in that country has failed to take some step legally available to them to secure the copyright (or other equivalent intellectual property right) in the work in that country:
the object is a copy in 3 dimensions of an artistic work that has been industrially applied in that country in the manner specified in section 75(4):
the object was made in that country by or with the consent of the owner of the copyright in the work in New Zealand.

blockList.listIntroduction: In this Act, an infringing copy does not include a literary work or an artistic work that—

item.p: relates to a medicine that has been imported by the Crown pursuant to section 32A of the Medicines Act 1981; and
has been made, copied, published, adapted, or distributed, in an overseas country, by or with the licence of the owner of the copyright in the work in that country.

section.heading: Act to bind the Crown

content.p: This Act binds the Crown.

part.heading: Description, ownership, and duration of copyright

section.heading: Copyright in original works

blockList.listIntroduction: Copyright is a property right that exists, in accordance with this Act, in original works of the following descriptions:

item.p: literary, dramatic, musical, or artistic works:
sound recordings:
films:
communication works:
typographical arrangements of published editions.

blockList.listIntroduction: A work is not original if—

item.p: it is, or to the extent that it is, a copy of another work; or
it infringes the copyright in, or to the extent that it infringes the copyright in, another work.

section.heading: Recording necessary for some works

content.p: Copyright does not exist in a literary or dramatic or musical work unless and until the work is recorded, in writing or otherwise.
It is immaterial for the purposes of subsection (1) whether the work is recorded by or with the consent of the author.
Where a work is not recorded by the author, the question whether copyright exists in the record, as distinct from the work recorded, is not affected by anything in subsection (1).

section.heading: Acts restricted by copyright

blockList.listIntroduction: The owner of the copyright in a work has the exclusive right to do, in accordance with sections 30 to 34, the following acts in New Zealand:

item.p: to copy the work:
to issue copies of the work to the public, whether by sale or otherwise:
to perform the work in public:
to play the work in public:
to show the work in public:
to communicate the work to the public:
to make an adaptation of the work:
to do any of the acts referred to in any of paragraphs (a) to (f) in relation to an adaptation of the work:
to authorise another person to do any of the acts referred to in any of paragraphs (a) to (h).

content.p: Subsection (1) applies subject to Parts 3 and 8.

section.heading: Qualification for copyright

content.p: Copyright does not exist in a work unless the requirements of section 18 or section 19 or section 20 are satisfied in respect of that work.
Subsection (1) does not apply to copyright that exists by virtue of section 26 or section 28.

If the requirements of section 18 or section 19 or section 20 or section 26 or section 28 are once satisfied in respect of a work, copyright in that work does not cease to exist if any change occurs in any of the circumstances by reason of which those requirements were satisfied.

For the avoidance of doubt, it is hereby declared that where any other provision of this Act imposes requirements, in addition to the requirements of section 18 or section 19 or section 20, that must be satisfied for copyright to exist in a work, copyright does not exist in a work unless the requirements of that provision and the requirements of section 18 or section 19 or section 20 are satisfied in respect of that work.

section.heading: Qualification by reference to author

blockList.listIntroduction: A work qualifies for copyright if the author is, at the material time,—

item.p: a New Zealand citizen; or
an individual domiciled or resident in New Zealand; or
a body incorporated under the law of New Zealand.

blockList.listIntroduction: A work qualifies for copyright if the author is, at the material time,—

item.p: a citizen or subject of a prescribed foreign country; or
an individual domiciled or resident in a prescribed foreign country; or
a body incorporated under the law of a prescribed foreign country.

content.p: Subject to subsection (4), a work of joint authorship qualifies for copyright if, at the material time, any of the authors satisfies the requirements of subsection (1) or subsection (2).

blockList.listIntroduction: Where a work of joint authorship qualifies for copyright under this section alone, only those authors who satisfy the requirements of subsection (1) or subsection (2) shall be taken into account for the purposes of the application, to that work, of the following provisions of this Act:

item.p: section 21 (which relates to the first ownership of copyright):
subsections (1) and (4) of section 22 (which relate to the duration of copyright in literary, dramatic, musical, or artistic works):
section 67 (which relates to acts permitted on assumptions as to expiry of copyright or death of the author in relation to anonymous or pseudonymous works).

section.heading: Qualification by reference to country of first publication

blockList.listIntroduction: A work (being a literary, dramatic, musical, or artistic work, a sound recording, a film, or a typographical arrangement of a published edition) qualifies for copyright if it is first published—

item.p: in New Zealand; or
in a prescribed foreign country.

content.p: For the purposes of this section, publication in one country shall not be regarded as other than the first publication by reason of simultaneous publication elsewhere; and for this purpose publication elsewhere within the previous 30 days shall be treated as simultaneous.

section.heading: Qualification by reference to origin of communication work

blockList.listIntroduction: A communication work qualifies for copyright if it is made from—

item.p: a place in New Zealand; or
a place in a prescribed foreign country.

section.heading: First ownership of copyright

content.p: Subject to the provisions of this section, the person who is the author of a work is the first owner of any copyright in the work.
Where an employee makes, in the course of his or her employment, a literary, dramatic, musical, or artistic work, that person's employer is the first owner of any copyright in the work.

blockList.listIntroduction: Where—

item.p: a person commissions, and pays or agrees to pay for, the taking of a photograph or the making of a computer program, painting, drawing, diagram, map, chart, plan, engraving, model, sculpture, film, or sound recording; and
the work is made in pursuance of that commission,—

content.p: that person is the first owner of any copyright in the work.
Subsections (2) and (3) apply subject to any agreement to the contrary.
Subsections (1) to (4) apply subject to sections 26 and 28.

section.heading: Duration of copyright in literary, dramatic, musical, or artistic works

content.p: Subject to the following provisions of this section, copyright in a literary, dramatic, musical, or artistic work expires at the end of the period of 50 years from the end of the calendar year in which the author dies.
If the work is computer-generated, copyright expires at the end of the period of 50 years from the end of the calendar year in which the work is made.
If the work is of unknown authorship, copyright expires at the end of the period of 50 years from the end of the calendar year in which it is first made available to the public by an authorised act.

blockList.listIntroduction: For the purposes of subsection (3), the circumstances in which a work may be made available to the public include,—

item.p: in the case of a literary, dramatic, or musical work,—
performance in public:
communication to the public:
in the case of an artistic work,—
exhibition in public:
the playing or showing in public of a film that includes the work:
communication to the public.

blockList.listIntroduction: If—

item.p: a work is of unknown authorship; and
copyright in the work has expired pursuant to subsection (3); and
the identity of the author becomes known after the copyright has expired,—

content.p: subsection (1) does not apply to revive copyright in the work.

blockList.listIntroduction: In relation to a work of joint authorship,—

item.p: the reference in subsection (1) to the death of the author shall be construed,—
if the identity of all the authors is known, as a reference to the last of them to die:
if the identity of 1 or more, but not all, of the authors is known, as a reference to the death of the last of the authors whose identity is known; and
the reference in subsection (5) to the identity of the author becoming known shall be construed as a reference to the identity of any of the authors becoming known.

content.p: This section does not apply to copyright in a work to which section 26 or section 28 applies.

section.heading: Duration of copyright in sound recordings and films

blockList.listIntroduction: Copyright in a sound recording or film expires—

item.p: at the end of the period of 50 years from the end of the calendar year in which the work is made; or
if it is made available to the public by an authorised act before the end of that period, 50 years from the end of the calendar year in which it is so made available,—

content.p: whichever is the later.

blockList.listIntroduction: For the purposes of subsection (1), a sound recording or film is made available to the public when—

item.p: the work is first—
published; or
communicated to the public; or
in the case of a film or film soundtrack,—
the work is first shown in public; or
the work is first played in public.

section.heading: Duration of copyright in communication works

content.p: Copyright in a communication work expires at the end of the period of 50 years from the end of the calendar year in which the communication work is first communicated to the public.
Copyright in a repeated communication work expires at the same time as copyright in the initial communication work expires.
There is no copyright in a repeated communication work that is communicated to the public after copyright in the initial communication work has expired.

section.heading: Duration of copyright in typographical arrangement of published editions

content.p: Copyright in a typographical arrangement of a published edition expires at the end of the period of 25 years from the end of the calendar year in which the edition is first published.

section.heading: Crown copyright

blockList.listIntroduction: Where a work is made by a person employed or engaged by the Crown under a contract of service, a contract of apprenticeship, or a contract for services,—

item.p: the work qualifies for copyright notwithstanding section 17(1); and
the Crown is the first owner of any copyright in the work.

content.p: Copyright in such a work is referred to in this Act as Crown copyright, notwithstanding that such copyright is assigned to another person.

blockList.listIntroduction: Crown copyright shall expire,—

item.p: in the case of a typographical arrangement of a published edition, at the end of the period of 25 years from the end of the calendar year in which the work is made:
in the case of any other work, at the end of the period of 100 years from the end of the calendar year in which the work is made.

content.p: In the case of a work of joint authorship where 1 or more, but not all, of the authors are persons employed or engaged by the Crown under a contract of service, a contract of apprenticeship, or a contract for services, this section applies only in relation to those authors and the copyright existing by virtue of their contribution to the work.
Subject to this section and to any other express provision of this Act, the provisions of this Act apply in relation to Crown copyright as to other copyright.
Subsection (1) applies subject to any agreement to the contrary.
This section is subject to section 27.

section.heading: No copyright in certain works

blockList.listIntroduction: No copyright exists in any of the following works, whenever those works were made:

item.p: any Bill introduced into the House of Representatives:
any Act:
any regulations:
the New Zealand Parliamentary Debates:
reports of select committees laid before the House of Representatives:
judgments of any court or tribunal:
reports of Royal commissions, commissions of inquiry, ministerial inquiries, or statutory inquiries; or
reports of any inquiry established under section 6 of the Inquiries Act 2013.

blockList.listIntroduction: No Crown copyright exists in any work, whenever that work was made,—

item.p: in which the Crown copyright has not been assigned to another person; and
that is incorporated by reference in a work referred to in subsection (1).

content.p: Except as specified in subsection (1A), nothing in subsection (1) affects copyright in any work that is incorporated by reference in a work referred to in subsection (1).
Subsection (1A) does not affect copyright in any New Zealand Standard (as that term is defined in the Standards and Accreditation Act 2015).

Subsection (1) shall come into force on a date to be appointed by the Governor-General by Order in Council; and 1 or more Orders in Council may be made appointing different dates for different paragraphs of that subsection.
An order under this section is secondary legislation (see Part 3 of the Legislation Act 2019 for publication requirements).

section.heading: Copyright vesting in certain international organisations

blockList.listIntroduction: Where an original work (being a literary, dramatic, musical, or artistic work or a film) is made by an officer or employee of, or is published by, an international organisation to which this section applies,—

item.p: the work qualifies for copyright notwithstanding section 17(1); and
the organisation is the first owner of any copyright in the work.

blockList.listIntroduction: The copyright of an international organisation under this section shall expire,—

item.p: in the case of a typographical arrangement of a published edition, at the end of the period of 25 years from the end of the calendar year in which the work is made or such longer period as may be specified for the purposes of this paragraph pursuant to subsection (5):

in the case of any other work, at the end of the period of 50 years from the end of the calendar year in which the work is made or such longer period as may be specified for the purposes of this paragraph pursuant to subsection (5).

content.p: Subject to this section and to any other express provision of this Act, the provisions of this Act apply in relation to the copyright of an international organisation under this section.

An international organisation to which this section applies shall be deemed to have, and to have had at all material times, the legal capacities of a body corporate for the purposes of holding, dealing with, and enforcing copyright and in connection with all legal proceedings relating to copyright.

blockList.listIntroduction: The Governor-General may from time to time, by Order in Council,—

item.p: declare that any international organisation is an international organisation to which this section applies:
for the purposes of complying with any international obligation of New Zealand, specify a period for the purposes of paragraph (a) or paragraph (b) of subsection (2).

content.p: An order under this section is secondary legislation (see Part 3 of the Legislation Act 2019 for publication requirements).

section.heading: Infringement of copyright

content.p: Copyright in a work is infringed by a person who, other than pursuant to a copyright licence, does any restricted act.

blockList.listIntroduction: References in this Act to the doing of a restricted act are to the doing of that act—

item.p: in relation to the work as a whole or any substantial part of it; and
either directly or indirectly;—

content.p: and it is immaterial whether any intervening acts themselves infringe copyright.
This Part is subject to Parts 3 and 8.

section.heading: Infringement by copying

content.p: The copying of a work is a restricted act in relation to every description of copyright work.

section.heading: Infringement by issue of copies to public

content.p: The issue of copies of a work to the public is a restricted act in relation to every description of copyright work.

section.heading: Infringement by performance or playing or showing in public

content.p: The performance of a work in public is a restricted act only in relation to a literary, dramatic, or musical work.
The playing or showing of a work in public is a restricted act only in relation to a sound recording, film, or communication work.

blockList.listIntroduction: Where copyright in a work is infringed by the performance, playing, or showing of the work in public by means of apparatus for receiving visual images or sounds conveyed by electronic or other means,—

item.p: the person by whom the visual images or sounds are sent; and
in the case of a performance, the performers—

content.p: shall not be regarded as responsible for the infringement.
For the purposes of subsection (3), a person who sends visual images or sounds does not include a person who retransmits visual images or sounds.

section.heading: Infringement by communicating to public

content.p: Communicating a work to the public is a restricted act in relation to every description of copyright work.

section.heading: Infringement by making adaptation or act done in relation to adaptation

content.p: The making of an adaptation of a work is a restricted act only in relation to a literary, dramatic, or musical work.
For the purposes of subsection (1), an adaptation is made when it is recorded, in writing or otherwise.

The doing of any of the acts specified in any of sections 30 to 33 or in subsection (1), in relation to an adaptation of a work, is also a restricted act in relation to the literary, dramatic, or musical work from which the adaptation was made.

For the purposes of subsection (3), where the act done in relation to an adaptation of a work is an act specified in section 32 or section 33, it is immaterial whether the adaptation has been recorded, in writing or otherwise, at the time the act is done.

section.heading: Infringement by importation

blockList.listIntroduction: A person infringes copyright in a work if—

item.p: that person imports into New Zealand an object that is an infringing copy of the work and,—
in the case of a work that is a sound recording, film, or computer program to which subsection (6) applies, that person knows or ought reasonably to know that the object is an infringing copy; or
in the case of other works, that person knows or has reason to believe that the object is an infringing copy; and
the object was imported into New Zealand without a copyright licence; and
the object was imported into New Zealand other than for that person's private and domestic use.

blockList.listIntroduction: In civil proceedings for infringement of copyright under subsection (1), in the case of a work that is a sound recording, film, or computer program to which subsection (6) applies,—

item.p: an object is presumed to be an infringing copy in the absence of evidence to the contrary; and
the court must not require any person to disclose any information concerning the sources of supply of the object if it appears to the court that it is unreasonable to do so.

content.p: Subsections (3) and (4) are repealed on 31 October 2016.

blockList.listIntroduction: This subsection applies to the following sound recordings, films, and computer programs:

item.p: a sound recording stored in a material form that is separate from any device or apparatus capable of playing sound recordings:
a film produced principally for cinematic release, or a copy of that film, or a copy of a substantial part of that film:
a computer program stored in a material form that is separate from any device or apparatus capable of executing computer programs.

section.heading: Possessing or dealing with infringing copy

blockList.listIntroduction: Copyright in a work is infringed by a person who, in New Zealand, other than pursuant to a copyright licence,—

item.p: possesses in the course of a business; or
in the course of a business or otherwise, sells or lets for hire; or
in the course of a business, offers or exposes for sale or hire; or
in the course of a business, exhibits in public or distributes; or
distributes otherwise than in the course of a business to such an extent as to affect prejudicially the copyright owner—

content.p: an object that is, and that the person knows or has reason to believe is, an infringing copy of the work.

section.heading: Providing means for making infringing copies

blockList.listIntroduction: Copyright in a work is infringed by a person who, other than pursuant to a copyright licence,—

item.p: makes; or
imports into New Zealand; or
possesses in the course of a business; or
in the course of a business or otherwise, sells or lets for hire; or
in the course of a business, offers or exposes for sale or hire—

content.p: an object specifically designed or adapted for making copies of that work, knowing or having reason to believe that the object is to be used to make such infringing copies.

Copyright in a work is infringed by a person who, other than under a copyright licence, communicates a work to 1 or more persons, knowing or having reason to believe that infringing copies will be made by means of the reception of the communication in New Zealand or elsewhere.

section.heading: Permitting use of premises for infringing performance

content.p: Where copyright in a literary, dramatic, or musical work is infringed by a performance at a place of public entertainment, any person who gave permission for that place to be used for the performance is also liable for the infringement unless, when the person gave that permission, he or she believed on reasonable grounds that the performance would not infringe copyright.

In this section, the term place of public entertainment includes premises that are occupied mainly for purposes other than public entertainment but are from time to time made available for hire for the purposes of public entertainment.

section.heading: Provision of apparatus for infringing performance, etc

blockList.listIntroduction: Where copyright in a work is infringed by a performance of the work in public, or by the playing or showing of the work in public, by means of apparatus for—

item.p: playing sound recordings; or
showing films; or
receiving visual images or sounds conveyed by electronic means,—

content.p: the persons described in subsections (2) to (4) are also liable for the infringement.

blockList.listIntroduction: A person who supplied the apparatus, or any substantial part of it, is liable for the infringement if, when he or she supplied the apparatus or part,—

item.p: he or she knew, or had reason to believe, that the apparatus was likely to be so used as to infringe copyright; or

in the case of apparatus whose normal use involves a performance, playing, or showing in public, he or she had no reasonable grounds for believing that the apparatus would not be so used as to infringe copyright.

content.p: An occupier of premises who gave permission for the apparatus to be brought onto the premises is liable for the infringement if, when the occupier gave that permission, he or she knew, or had reason to believe, that the apparatus was likely to be so used as to infringe copyright.

A person who supplied a copy of a sound recording or film used to infringe copyright is liable for the infringement if, when the person supplied the copy, he or she knew, or had reason to believe, that the copy he or she supplied, or a copy made directly or indirectly from the copy, was likely to be so used as to infringe copyright.

part.heading: Acts permitted in relation to copyright works

section.heading: Provisions to be construed independently

content.p: The provisions of this Part are to be construed independently of one another so that the fact that an act is not permitted by one provision does not mean that it is not permitted by another provision.

section.heading: Incidental copying of copyright work

blockList.listIntroduction: Copyright in a work is not infringed by—

item.p: the incidental copying of the work in an artistic work, a sound recording, a film, or a communication work; or

the issue to the public of copies of an artistic work, the playing of a sound recording, the showing of a film, or the communication of a work to the public, in which a copyright work has been incidentally copied; or
the issue to the public of copies of a sound recording, film, or communication work to which paragraph (a) or (b) applies.

content.p: For the purposes of subsection (1), a musical work, words spoken or sung with music, or so much of a sound recording or communication work as includes a musical work or those words, must not be regarded as incidentally copied in another work if the musical work or the words, sound recording, or communication work is deliberately copied.

section.heading: Criticism, review, and news reporting

content.p: Fair dealing with a work for the purposes of criticism or review, of that or another work or of a performance of a work, does not infringe copyright in the work if such fair dealing is accompanied by a sufficient acknowledgement.
Fair dealing with a work for the purpose of reporting current events by means of a sound recording, film, or communication work does not infringe copyright in the work.

Fair dealing with a work (other than a photograph) for the purposes of reporting current events by any means other than those referred to in subsection (2) does not infringe copyright in the work if such fair dealing is accompanied by a sufficient acknowledgement.

section.heading: Research or private study

content.p: Fair dealing with a work for the purposes of research or private study does not infringe copyright in the work.

For the avoidance of doubt, it is hereby declared that fair dealing with a published edition for the purposes of research or private study does not infringe copyright in either the typographical arrangement of the edition or any literary, dramatic, musical, or artistic work or part of a work in the edition.

blockList.listIntroduction: In determining, for the purposes of subsection (1), whether copying, by means of a reprographic process or by any other means, constitutes fair dealing for the purposes of research or private study, a court shall have regard to—

item.p: the purpose of the copying; and
the nature of the work copied; and
whether the work could have been obtained within a reasonable time at an ordinary commercial price; and
the effect of the copying on the potential market for, or value of, the work; and
where part of a work is copied, the amount and substantiality of the part copied taken in relation to the whole work.

content.p: This section does not authorise the making of more than 1 copy of the same work, or the same part of a work, on any one occasion, but in this subsection copy does not include a non-infringing transient reproduction to which section 43A applies.

section.heading: Transient reproduction of work

blockList.listIntroduction: A reproduction of a work does not infringe copyright in the work if the reproduction—

item.p: is transient or incidental; and
is an integral and essential part of a technological process for—
making or receiving a communication that does not infringe copyright; or
enabling the lawful use of, or lawful dealing in, the work; and
has no independent economic significance.

section.heading: Copying for educational purposes of literary, dramatic, musical or artistic works or typographical arrangements

blockList.listIntroduction: Copyright in a literary, dramatic, musical, or artistic work or the typographical arrangement of a published edition is not infringed by the copying of the whole or part of the work or edition if—

item.p: the copying is done by means of a reprographic process or by any other means; and
the copying is done—
in the course of preparation for instruction; or
for use in the course of instruction; or
in the course of instruction; and
the copying is done by or on behalf of the person who is to give, or who is giving, a lesson at an educational establishment; and
no more than 1 copy of the whole or part of the work or edition is made on any one occasion.

blockList.listIntroduction: Copyright in a literary, dramatic, musical, or artistic work or the typographical arrangement of a published edition is not infringed by the copying of the whole or part of the work or edition if—

item.p: the copying is not done by means of a reprographic process; and
the copying is done—
in the course of preparation for instruction; or
for use in the course of instruction; or
in the course of instruction; or
after the course of instruction; and
the copying is done by a person who is to give, is giving, or has given the lesson or by a person who is to receive, is receiving, or has received the lesson; and
1 or more copies of the whole or part of the work or edition is or are made on any one occasion.

blockList.listIntroduction: Copyright in a literary, dramatic, or musical work or the typographical arrangement of a published edition is not infringed by the copying of part of the work or edition if—

item.p: the copying is done by means of a reprographic process or by any other means; and
the copying is done for an educational purpose; and
the copying is done by or on behalf of an educational establishment; and
1 or more copies of part of the work or edition is or are made on any one occasion; and
no charge is made for the supply of a copy to any student or other person who is to receive, is receiving, or has received a lesson; and
subject to subsection (4), either,—

in the period beginning with the commencement of this Act and ending with the close of 31 December 1997, the copying is of no more than the greater of 5% of the work or edition or 5 pages of the work or edition; or
on and after 1 January 1998, the copying is of no more than the greater of 3% of the work or edition or 3 pages of the work or edition.

content.p: If the effect of subparagraph (i) or subparagraph (ii) of subsection (3)﻿(f) would be that the whole of a work or edition is copied, those subparagraphs shall not apply and the copying that is permitted under subsection (3) shall be of no more than 50% of the whole work or edition.

A copy of a work made in accordance with subsections (3) and (4) may be communicated to a person who is a student or other person who is to receive, is receiving, or has received, a lesson that relates to the work.

Copyright in an artistic work is not infringed by the copying, by means of a reprographic process or by any other means, of the whole or a part of that work if the artistic work is included within the part of any work or edition copied under subsection (3).

blockList.listIntroduction: Where any part of a work or edition is copied under subsection (3) by or on behalf of an educational establishment,—

item.p: that part of that work or edition may not, within 14 days of that copying, be copied again under that subsection by or on behalf of that educational establishment; and
no other part of that work or edition may, within 14 days of that copying, be copied under that subsection by or on behalf of that educational establishment.

content.p: In subsections (3) to (6),—

section.heading: Storing copies for educational purposes

blockList.listIntroduction: An educational establishment does not infringe copyright in a work that is made available on a website or other electronic retrieval system by storing a copy of the page or pages in which the work appears if—

item.p: the material is stored for an educational purpose; and
the material—
is displayed under a separate frame or identifier; and
identifies the author (if known) and source of the work; and
states the name of the educational establishment and the date on which the work was stored; and
the material is restricted to use by authenticated users.

content.p: Subsection (1) does not apply, and the educational establishment does infringe copyright in the work, if the educational establishment knowingly fails to delete the stored material within a reasonable time after the material becomes no longer relevant to the course of instruction for which it was stored.

blockList.listIntroduction: In subsection (1), authenticated user means a person who—

item.p: is a participant in the course of instruction for which the material is stored; and
can access the stored material only through a verification process that verifies that he or she is entitled to access the stored material.

section.heading: Copying for educational purposes of films and sound recordings

content.p: Copyright in any work that is a film, sound recording, or communication work, or any work included in a film, sound recording, or communication work, is not infringed by the copying of that work in the circumstances set out in subsection (2).

blockList.listIntroduction: The circumstances referred to in subsection (1) are—

item.p: that the copying consists of or includes the making of a film or film soundtrack— where the lesson is on how to make films or film soundtracks; and
in the course of preparation for instruction; or
for use in the course of instruction; or
in the course of instruction; or
after the course of instruction,—
that the copying is done by or on behalf of a person who is to give, is giving, or has given the lesson or by or on behalf of a person who is to receive, is receiving, or has received the lesson; and
that no charge is made for the supply of a copy to any student or other person who is to receive, is receiving, or has received the lesson.

blockList.listIntroduction: Copyright in—

item.p: any work that is a sound recording; or
any work included in a sound recording—

content.p: is not infringed by the copying of that work in the circumstances set out in subsection (4).

blockList.listIntroduction: The circumstances referred to in subsection (3) are—

item.p: that the copying is done— where the lesson—
in the course of preparation for instruction; or
for use in the course of instruction; or
in the course of instruction; or
after the course of instruction,—
relates to the learning of a language; or
is conducted by correspondence; and
that the copying is done by or on behalf of a person who is to give, is giving, or has given the lesson or by or on behalf of a person who is to receive, is receiving, or has received the lesson; and
that no charge is made for the supply of a copy to any student or other person who is to receive, is receiving, or has received the lesson.

content.p: Subsections (3) and (4) do not apply if or to the extent that licences authorising the copying of a work in the circumstances set out in subsection (4) are available under a licensing scheme and the person doing the copying knew that fact.

section.heading: Anthologies for educational use

blockList.listIntroduction: The copying of a short passage from a published work (being a literary, dramatic, or musical work) in a collection that—

item.p: is intended for use in educational establishments and is so described in its title, and in any advertisements issued by or on behalf of the publisher of that collection; and
consists mainly of material in which no copyright exists or in which copyright is owned by the publisher of that collection or the Crown—

blockList.listIntroduction: does not infringe copyright in the work if—

item.p: the publisher of the work did not intend it to be used in such establishments; and
the passage is accompanied by a sufficient acknowledgement.

content.p: Subsection (1) does not authorise the copying of more than 2 passages from copyright works by the same author in collections published by the same publisher over any period of 5 years.

blockList.listIntroduction: In relation to any given passage, the reference in subsection (2) to passages from copyright works by the same author—

item.p: shall be taken to include passages from collective works of which that author is one of the authors; and
if the passage in question is from such a collective work, shall be taken to include passages from works by any of the authors, whether alone or in collaboration with another.

content.p: References in this section to the use of a work in an educational establishment are to any use for the educational purposes of such an establishment.
Subsection (1) does not apply to a literary work that is a computer program.

section.heading: Performing, playing, or showing work in course of activities of educational establishment

blockList.listIntroduction: The performance of a literary, dramatic, or musical work before an audience consisting of persons who are students or staff members at an educational establishment or are directly connected with the activities of the establishment—

item.p: by a student or staff member in the course of the activities of the establishment; or
at the establishment, by any person for the purposes of instruction,—

content.p: is not a performance in public for the purposes of section 32(1).

The playing or showing, for the purposes of instruction, of a sound recording, film, or communication work to the audience described in subsection (1) at an educational establishment is not a playing or showing of the work in public for the purposes of section 32(2).

For the purposes of this section, a person shall not be treated as a person directly connected with the activities of an educational establishment by reason only that the person is a parent or guardian of a student at that educational establishment.

section.heading: Copying and communication of communication work for educational purposes

blockList.listIntroduction: This section applies when a copy of a communication work is—

item.p: made or communicated by or on behalf of an educational establishment; or
made and supplied by an educational resource supplier to an educational establishment.

content.p: In any case to which subsection (1)﻿(a) applies, the making or communication of a copy of the communication work by or on behalf of an educational establishment, and the subsequent communication of the copy within the educational establishment, does not infringe copyright in the communication work or in any work included in it if the copy is made or communicated for the educational establishment’s educational purposes.

In any case to which subsection (1)﻿(b) applies, the making and supply of a copy of the communication work by an educational resource supplier does not infringe copyright in the communication work or in any work included in it if the copy is made and supplied for the educational purposes of the educational establishment to which it is supplied.

blockList.listIntroduction: However, the exclusions from infringement of copyright in subsections (2) and (3) do not apply to—

item.p: the copying of a communication work if or to the extent that—
licences authorising the copying of the communication work by or on behalf of educational establishments or by educational resource suppliers are available under a licensing scheme; and
the educational establishment or the educational resource supplier, as the case may be, knew that fact; or
the communication of a communication work if or to the extent that—
licences authorising the communication of the copy by or on behalf of educational establishments are available under a licensing scheme; and
the educational establishment knew that fact; or
the supply of a communication work by an educational resource supplier if or to the extent that—
licences authorising the supply of the communication work are available under a licensing scheme; and
the educational resource supplier knew that fact.

section.heading: Things done for purposes of examination

content.p: Copyright is not infringed by anything done for the purposes of an examination, whether by way of setting the questions, communicating the questions to the candidates, or answering the questions.

section.heading: Interpretation

content.p: In sections 51 to 56C, unless the context otherwise requires,—
In sections 51 to 56C, every reference to the librarian of a prescribed library or the archivist of an archive shall be read as including a person acting on behalf of the librarian or archivist.

section.heading: Copying by librarians of parts of published works

content.p: The librarian of a prescribed library may, if the conditions contained in subsection (2) are complied with, make from a published edition (other than a published edition that is an article in a periodical), for supply to any person, a copy of a reasonable proportion of any literary, dramatic, or musical work, and may include in the copy any artistic work that appears within the proportion copied, without infringing copyright in the literary, dramatic, musical, or artistic work or the typographical arrangement of the published edition.

blockList.listIntroduction: The conditions referred to in subsection (1) are—

item.p: that no person is supplied on the same occasion with more than 1 copy of the same material; and

that, where any person to whom a copy is supplied is required to pay for the copy, the payment required is no higher than a sum consisting of the total of the cost of production of the copy and a reasonable contribution to the general expenses of the library.

content.p: Where any person is supplied with, or otherwise comes into possession of, a copy made in accordance with this section, that person may use the copy only for the purposes of research or private study.
This section does not apply to a literary work that is a computer program.
In this section, copy includes a digital copy, but in that case section 56B applies as well.

section.heading: Copying by librarians of articles in periodicals

blockList.listIntroduction: The librarian of a prescribed library may, if the conditions contained in subsection (2) are complied with, make for supply to any person a copy of—

item.p: a literary, dramatic, or musical work, and any artistic work included in that work, that is contained in an article in a periodical; or
a published edition that is an article in a periodical,—

content.p: without infringing copyright in the literary, dramatic, musical, or artistic work or the typographical arrangement of the published edition.

blockList.listIntroduction: The conditions referred to in subsection (1) are—

item.p: that no person is supplied on the same occasion with more than 1 copy of the same article; and
that no person is supplied on the same occasion with copies of more than 1 article contained in the same issue of a periodical, unless the copies supplied all relate to the same subject matter; and

that, where any person to whom a copy is supplied is required to pay for the copy, the payment required is no higher than a sum consisting of the total of the cost of production of the copy and a reasonable contribution to the general expenses of the library.

content.p: Where any person is supplied with, or otherwise comes into possession of, a copy made in accordance with this section, that person may use the copy only for the purposes of research or private study.
In this section, copy includes a digital copy, but in that case section 56B applies as well.

section.heading: Copying by librarians for users of other libraries

blockList.listIntroduction: The librarian of a prescribed library may, if the condition contained in subsection (2) is complied with, make from a published edition, for supply to another prescribed library, a copy of,—

item.p: subject to paragraph (b), a reasonable proportion of any literary, dramatic, or musical work (and the librarian may include in the copy any artistic work that appears within the proportion copied):
in relation to a literary, dramatic, or musical work that is contained in an article in a periodical,—
the whole article and any artistic work included in that article; and

if there is any other article in the same issue of the periodical relating to the same subject matter as the first article copied, the whole of that other article and any artistic work included in that article,—

content.p: without infringing copyright in the literary, dramatic, musical, or artistic work or the typographical arrangement of the published edition.

The condition referred to in subsection (1) is that a person has requested the library to which the copy is being supplied to supply him or her with the copy for the purposes of research or private study.
Where any person is supplied with, or otherwise comes into possession of, a copy made in accordance with this section, that person may use the copy only for the purposes of research or private study.
This section does not apply to a literary work that is a computer program.
In this section, copy includes a digital copy, but in that case section 56C applies as well.

section.heading: Copying by librarians for collections of other libraries

blockList.listIntroduction: The librarian of a prescribed library may, if the conditions contained in subsection (2) are complied with, make a copy of a literary, dramatic, or musical work and any artistic work included in the work, where the copy is—

item.p: from a published edition that is a book; and
for supply to the librarian of another prescribed library,—

content.p: without infringing copyright in the literary, dramatic, musical, or artistic work or the typographical arrangement of the published edition.

blockList.listIntroduction: The conditions referred to in subsection (1) are that the librarian to whom the copy of the work is supplied—

item.p: has been unable to obtain the work at an ordinary commercial price within the 6 months preceding the supply; and
makes and keeps a record sufficient to identify the work copied; and
permits the inspection of the record by the copyright owner during normal office hours; and
pays, on demand, equitable remuneration to the copyright owner for the work copied.

content.p: In subsection (2)﻿(d), the term equitable remuneration means a sum agreed by the librarian and the copyright owner or, in the absence of agreement, a sum determined by the Tribunal on an application under section 168.
This section does not apply to a literary work that is a computer program.
In this section, copy includes a digital copy, but in that case section 56C applies as well.

section.heading: Copying by librarians or archivists to replace copies of works

blockList.listIntroduction: The librarian of a prescribed library or the archivist of an archive may make a copy (other than a digital copy) of any item in the collection of the library or archive for the purposes of—

item.p: preserving or replacing that item by placing the copy in the collection of the library or archive in addition to or in place of the item; or
replacing in the collection of another prescribed library or archive an item that has been lost, destroyed, or damaged,—

content.p: without infringing copyright in any work included in the item.
Subsection (1) applies only where it is not reasonably practicable to purchase a copy of the item in question to fulfil the purpose.

blockList.listIntroduction: The librarian of a prescribed library or the archivist of an archive may make a digital copy of any item (the original item) in the collection of the library or archive without infringing copyright in any work included in the item if—

item.p: the original item is at risk of loss, damage, or destruction; and
the digital copy replaces the original item; and

the original item is not accessible by members of the public after replacement by the digital copy except for purposes of research the nature of which requires or may benefit from access to the original item; and
it is not reasonably practicable to purchase a copy of the original item.

blockList.listIntroduction: The librarian of a prescribed library or the archivist of an archive may make a digital copy of any item (the original item) in the collection of the library or archive without infringing copyright in any work included in the item if—

item.p: the digital copy is used to replace an item in the collection of another prescribed library or archive that has been lost, damaged, or destroyed; and
it is not reasonably practicable to purchase a copy of the original item.

section.heading: Copying by librarians or archivists of certain unpublished works

content.p: The librarian of a prescribed library or the archivist of an archive may, if the conditions contained in subsection (3) are complied with, copy for supply to any person a copy of an unpublished work in the library or archive, without infringing copyright in that work.
This section does not apply if the copyright owner has prohibited copying of the work and at the time the copy is made the librarian or archivist making it is, or ought to be, aware of that fact.

blockList.listIntroduction: The conditions referred to in subsection (1) are—

item.p: that no person is supplied on the same occasion with more than 1 copy of the same work; and

that, where any person to whom a copy is supplied is required to pay for the copy, the payment required is no higher than a sum consisting of the total of the cost of production of the copy and a reasonable contribution to the general expenses of the library or archive.

content.p: Where any person is supplied with, or otherwise comes into possession of, a copy made in accordance with this section, that person may use the copy only for the purposes of research or private study.

The provisions of this section do not apply to the sound archive maintained by Radio New Zealand Limited, the film archive maintained by Television New Zealand Limited, or the film archive maintained by the New Zealand Film Archive Incorporated.
In this section, copy includes a digital copy, but in that case section 56B applies as well.

section.heading: Library or archive may communicate digital copy to authenticated users

blockList.listIntroduction: The librarian of a prescribed library or the archivist of an archive does not infringe copyright in a work by communicating a digital copy of the work to an authenticated user if the following conditions are met:

item.p: the librarian or archivist has obtained the digital copy lawfully; and

the librarian or archivist ensures that each user is informed in writing about the limits of copying and communication allowed by this Act, including that a digital copy of a work may only be copied or communicated by the user in accordance with the provisions of this Act; and
the digital copy is communicated to the user in a form that cannot be altered or modified; and
the number of users who access the digital copy at any one time is not more than the aggregate number of digital copies of the work that—
the library or the archive has purchased; or
for which it is licensed.

blockList.listIntroduction: In subsection (1), authenticated user means a person who—

item.p: has a legitimate right to use the services of the library or archive; and
can access the digital copy only through a verification process that verifies that the person is entitled to access the digital copy.

section.heading: Additional conditions for supply of copy of work in digital format by librarian or archivist under section 51, 52, or 56

blockList.listIntroduction: A copy of a work to which section 51, 52, or 56 applies must not be supplied in a digital format, by the librarian of a prescribed library or the archivist of an archive, to a person (A) unless the following conditions are also complied with:

item.p: the librarian or archivist must give A, when the copy is supplied, a written notice that sets out the terms of use of the copy; and
the librarian or archivist must, as soon as is reasonably practicable, destroy any additional copy made in the process of making the copy that is supplied to A.

section.heading: Additional condition for making digital copies under section 53 or 54

content.p: A copy of a work to which section 53 or 54 applies must not be supplied in a digital format to a library unless the librarian supplying the digital copy destroys, as soon as is reasonably practicable, any additional copy made in the process of making the copy that is supplied.

section.heading: Playing or showing sound recordings or films

content.p: The sound archive maintained by Radio New Zealand Limited may play a sound recording held in the archive to an audience consisting of members of the public, without infringing copyright in the sound recording or in any work included in the sound recording, if the condition contained in subsection (3) is complied with.

The film archive maintained by Television New Zealand Limited or by the New Zealand Film Archive Incorporated may show a film, and play any sound recording associated with the film, held in the archive to an audience consisting of members of the public, without infringing copyright in the film or in any sound recording associated with the film or in any work included in the film or sound recording, if the condition contained in subsection (3) is complied with.

blockList.listIntroduction: The condition referred to in subsections (1) and (2) is that, where any person is required to pay to—

item.p: hear any sound recording played under subsection (1); or
see any film shown, and hear any sound recording associated with the film played, under subsection (2),—

content.p: the payment required is no more than a reasonable contribution towards the maintenance of the archive in which the sound recording or film is held.

This section does not apply if or to the extent that licences authorising the playing of a sound recording, or the showing of a film and the playing of a sound recording associated with the film, by an archive to which this section applies are available and if the archive knew that fact.

section.heading: Making archived works available for public viewing

content.p: The communication of an archived work in accordance with section 29C of the Television New Zealand Act 2003 does not infringe copyright (if any) in the archived work under this Act.
In this section, archived work has the same meaning as in section 29A of the Television New Zealand Act 2003.

section.heading: Copying by Parliamentary Service for members of Parliament

content.p: An employee of the Parliamentary Service may, if the conditions contained in subsection (3) are complied with, supply to any member of Parliament a copy of a literary or dramatic work, and any artistic work included in that work, without infringing copyright in that literary, dramatic, or artistic work or the typographical arrangement of a published edition.

An employee of the Parliamentary Service may, if the conditions contained in subsection (3) are complied with, supply to any member of Parliament a recording of a communication work or a transcript of a recording of the communication work, without infringing copyright in the communication work or any work included in that communication work.

blockList.listIntroduction: The conditions referred to in subsections (1) and (2) are—

item.p: that the employee of the Parliamentary Service is engaged in supplying the library, information, research, and reference services provided by the Parliamentary Service under section 123(1)﻿(e) of the Parliament Act 2025; and
that no member of Parliament is supplied on the same occasion with more than 1 copy or recording or transcript, as the case may be, of the same material; and
that the copy or recording or transcript is required by that member of Parliament for the purposes of performing his or her duties as such a member.

section.heading: Parliamentary and judicial proceedings

content.p: Copyright is not infringed by anything done for the purposes of parliamentary or judicial proceedings.
Copyright is not infringed by anything done for the purposes of reporting parliamentary or judicial proceedings.

section.heading: Royal commissions and statutory inquiries

content.p: Copyright is not infringed by anything done for the purposes of the proceedings of a Royal commission, commission of inquiry, ministerial inquiry, or statutory inquiry.

Copyright is not infringed by anything done for the purposes of reporting any proceedings of a Royal commission, commission of inquiry, ministerial inquiry, or statutory inquiry that are held in public.

Copyright in a work is not infringed by the issue to the public of copies of the report of a Royal commission, commission of inquiry, ministerial inquiry, or statutory inquiry containing the work or material from it.

section.heading: Material open to public inspection or on official register

content.p: Subject to any Order in Council made under subsection (4), where material is open to public inspection or public reference pursuant to a statutory requirement, or is on a statutory register, copyright in the material is not infringed by the copying of the material, by or with the authority of the appropriate person, for a purpose that does not involve the issuing of copies to the public.

Subject to any Order in Council made under subsection (4), where material is open to public inspection or public reference pursuant to a statutory requirement, copyright is not infringed by the copying or issuing to the public of copies of the material, by or with the authority of the appropriate person, for the purpose of enabling the material to be inspected at a more convenient time or place or otherwise facilitating the exercise of any right for the purpose of which the requirement is imposed.

Subject to any Order in Council made under subsection (4), where material that is open to public inspection or public reference pursuant to a statutory requirement, or that is on a statutory register, contains information about matters of general scientific, technical, commercial, or economic interest, copyright is not infringed by the copying or issuing to the public of copies of the material, by or with the authority of the appropriate person, for the purpose of disseminating that information.

The Governor-General may from time to time, by Order in Council, provide that all or any of subsections (1) to (3) shall, in such cases as may be specified in the order, apply only to copies marked in such manner as may be so specified.

blockList.listIntroduction: The Governor-General may from time to time, by Order in Council, provide that all or any of subsections (1) to (3) apply, to such extent and with such modifications as may be specified in the order, in relation to—

item.p: material made open to public inspection or public reference by—
an international organisation specified in the order; or
a person specified in the order who has functions in New Zealand under an international agreement to which New Zealand is a party; or
a register maintained by an international organisation specified in the order,—

content.p: as those provisions apply in relation to material open to public inspection or public reference pursuant to a statutory requirement or by virtue of being on a statutory register.
In this section,—
An order under this section is secondary legislation (see Part 3 of the Legislation Act 2019 for publication requirements).

section.heading: Material communicated to the Crown in course of public business

blockList.listIntroduction: This section applies where—

item.p: a literary, dramatic, musical, or artistic work has, in the course of public business, been communicated to the Crown for any purpose, by or with the licence of the copyright owner; and
a document (within the meaning of section 2 of the Official Information Act 1982) recording or embodying the work is owned by, or is in the custody or control of, the Crown.

blockList.listIntroduction: The Crown may, for—

item.p: the purpose for which the work was communicated to the Crown; or
any related purpose that could reasonably have been anticipated by the copyright owner,—

content.p: copy the work, and issue copies of the work to the public, without infringing copyright in the work.
The Crown may not copy a work, or issue copies of a work to the public, under this section if the work has previously been published otherwise than under this section.
In subsection (1), the term public business includes any activity carried on by the Crown.
This section has effect subject to any agreement to the contrary between the Crown and the copyright owner.

section.heading: Use of copyright material for services of the Crown

blockList.listIntroduction: Copyright in a work is not infringed by anything done in relation to the work, by or on behalf of the Crown or any person authorised in writing by a government department,—

item.p: for the purpose of national security or during a period of emergency; or
in the interests of the safety or health of the public or any members of the public.

content.p: Where any act is done under subsection (1), the Crown shall be liable to pay, out of money appropriated by Parliament for the purpose, equitable remuneration to the copyright owner upon such terms as may be agreed upon between the Crown and the copyright owner or, in the absence of agreement, upon such terms as shall be determined by the Tribunal.

blockList.listIntroduction: No act to which subsection (1) applies shall—

item.p: constitute publication of a work; or
affect the term of copyright in a work.

section.heading: Rights of third parties in respect of Crown use

content.p: No provision of any assignment or licence in force between the copyright owner and a person other than a government department shall be effective to prevent any act being done in relation to a copyright work, where that act is done under section 63.

blockList.listIntroduction: Where—

item.p: an act is done under section 63; and
an exclusive licence is in force in respect of the work in relation to which the act is done,—

content.p: the Crown shall be liable to pay, out of money appropriated by Parliament for the purpose, equitable remuneration to the licensee upon such terms as may be agreed between the Crown and the licensee or, in the absence of agreement, upon such terms as shall be determined by the Tribunal.

blockList.listIntroduction: Where—

item.p: a person has a right in relation to a work, by any licence other than an exclusive licence; and
a payment is made, in respect of that work, under section 63 to the copyright owner or under subsection (2) to the exclusive licensee,—

content.p: the person is entitled to recover from the owner or exclusive licensee, as the case may be, such part of any payment as may be agreed between that person and the copyright owner or the exclusive licensee, as the case may be, or, in the absence of agreement, as shall be determined by the Tribunal.

section.heading: Proceedings against the Crown

content.p: Where any employee or agent of the Crown infringes copyright in a work, and the infringement is committed with the authority of the Crown, civil proceedings in respect of the infringement shall, subject to this Act, lie against the Crown under the Crown Proceedings Act 1950.
Nothing in subsection (1) shall affect the rights of the Crown, or any person authorised by a government department, under section 63.

section.heading: Acts done under statutory authority

content.p: Where the doing of a particular act is specifically authorised by an enactment, the doing of that act does not infringe copyright, unless the enactment provides otherwise.
Nothing in this section shall be construed as excluding any defence of statutory authority otherwise available under or pursuant to any enactment.

hcontainer.name: crossHeading
hcontainer.heading: Literary, dramatic, musical, or artistic works

section.heading: Acts permitted on assumptions as to expiry of copyright or death of author in relation to anonymous or pseudonymous works

blockList.listIntroduction: Copyright in a literary, dramatic, musical, or artistic work is not infringed by any act done at a time when, or in pursuance of arrangements made at a time when,—

item.p: it is not possible for a person who wishes to do so to ascertain the identity of the author by reasonable inquiry; and
it is reasonable to assume—
that copyright has expired; or
that the author died 50 years or more before the beginning of the calendar year in which the act is done or the arrangements are made.

blockList.listIntroduction: Subsection (1)﻿(b)﻿(ii) does not apply in relation to—

item.p: a work in which Crown copyright exists under section 26; or
a work—
in which copyright originally vested in an international organisation under section 28; and
in respect of which an order made under that section specifies a copyright period longer than 50 years.

blockList.listIntroduction: In relation to a work of joint authorship,—

item.p: the reference in subsection (1)﻿(a) to its being possible to ascertain the identity of the author shall be construed as a reference to its being possible to ascertain the identity of any of the authors; and
the reference in subsection (1)﻿(b)﻿(ii) to the author having died shall be construed as a reference to all the authors having died.

section.heading: Use of recording of spoken words in certain cases

blockList.listIntroduction: Where a recording of spoken words is made, in writing or otherwise, for the purpose of—

item.p: reporting current events; or
communicating to the public the whole or part of the work,—

content.p: it is not an infringement of copyright in the words as a literary work to use the recording or material taken from it (or to copy the recording, or any such material, and use the copy) for that purpose, if the conditions in subsection (2) are complied with.

blockList.listIntroduction: The conditions referred to in subsection (1) are that—

item.p: the recording is a direct record of the spoken words and is not taken from a previous recording or from a communication work; and
the making of the recording was not prohibited by the speaker and, where copyright already existed in the work, did not infringe copyright; and
the use made of the recording or material taken from it is not of a kind prohibited by or on behalf of the speaker or copyright owner before the recording was made; and
the use is by or with the authority of a person who is lawfully in possession of the recording.

section.heading: Authorised entity types

blockList.listIntroduction: An entity that is 1 or more of the following may undertake the activities set out in section 69A:

item.p: an educational establishment:
an educational resource supplier:
a prescribed library within the meaning given in section 50(1):
a charitable entity that has a purpose consistent with making accessible format copies available to persons who have a print disability.

content.p: Before beginning activities under section 69A for the first time, an authorised entity must give notice to the Ministry that it intends to do so.

section.heading: Accessible format copy activities by authorised entity

content.p: An authorised entity does not infringe copyright in the relevant work if the entity acts in accordance with this section.

blockList.listIntroduction: An authorised entity may make an accessible format copy if the entity—

item.p: has taken all reasonable steps to notify the owner of the copyright in the work of its intention to make an accessible format copy; and
is making the copy to provide it only to persons who have a print disability, persons acting on their behalf, or other authorised entities; and
ensures that the copy respects the integrity of the original work, as far as is reasonably possible and taking into account changes needed to make the work accessible in the alternative format.

blockList.listIntroduction: An authorised entity (A) may import into New Zealand an accessible format copy from an authorised entity (B) in another Marrakesh Treaty country if A—

item.p: has taken all reasonable steps to notify the owner of the copyright in the work of its intention to make an accessible format copy; and
is importing the copy to provide it only to persons who have a print disability, persons acting on their behalf, or other authorised entities; and

has taken all reasonable steps to ensure that the copy respects the integrity of the original work, as far as is reasonably possible and taking into account changes needed to make the work accessible in the alternative format.

blockList.listIntroduction: An authorised entity may do 1 or more of the following:
