The issuer of the TPM work has the same rights under section 122 (order for delivery up in civil proceedings) or 132 (order for delivery up in criminal proceedings) in relation to a TPM circumvention device as a copyright owner has in relation to an infringing copy.
Sections 126 to 129 and 197A (which relate to certain presumptions) apply in relation to proceedings under this section.
Section 134 (order as to disposal of infringing copy or other object) applies, with all necessary modifications, in relation to the disposal of anything that is delivered up under subsection (3).

blockList.listIntroduction: A performer (A) must be treated as an issuer of the TPM work for the purposes of this section if—

item.p: the performance is fixed in a sound recording; and
the TPM work is the sound recording; and
A issued a copy of the TPM work to the public or communicated the TPM work to the public.

section.heading: Offence of contravening section 226A

content.p: A person (A) commits an offence who, in the course of business, makes, imports, sells, distributes, lets for hire, offers or exposes for sale or hire, or advertises for sale or hire, a TPM circumvention device that applies to a technological protection measure if A knows that it will, or is likely to, be used to infringe copyright in a TPM work.

blockList.listIntroduction: A person (A) commits an offence who, in the course of business, provides a service to another person (B) if—

item.p: A intends the service to enable or assist B to circumvent a technological protection measure; and
A knows that the service will, or is likely to, be used to infringe copyright in a TPM work.

content.p: A person (A) commits an offence who, in the course of business, publishes information enabling or assisting another person to circumvent a technological protection measure if A intends that the information will be used to infringe copyright in a TPM work.
A person who commits an offence under this section is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $150,000 or a term of imprisonment not exceeding 5 years or both.

section.heading: When rights of issuer of TPM work do not apply

content.p: The rights that the issuer of a TPM work has under section 226B do not prevent or restrict the exercise of a permitted act.

blockList.listIntroduction: The rights that the issuer of a TPM work has under section 226B do not prevent or restrict the making, importation, sale, or letting for hire of a TPM circumvention device to enable—

item.p: a qualified person to exercise a permitted act using a TPM circumvention device on behalf of the user of a TPM work; or
a person referred to in section 226E(3) to undertake encryption research.

blockList.listIntroduction: In this section and in section 226E, qualified person means—

item.p: the librarian of a prescribed library; or
the archivist of an archive; or
an educational establishment; or
any other person specified by the Governor-General by Order in Council on the recommendation of the Minister.

content.p: A qualified person must not be supplied with a TPM circumvention device on behalf of a user unless the qualified person has first made a declaration to the supplier in the prescribed form.
In this section,—
In this section and in section 226E, encryption research means identifying and analysing flaws and vulnerabilities of encryption technology.
An order under subsection (3)﻿(d) is secondary legislation (see Part 3 of the Legislation Act 2019 for publication requirements).

section.heading: User’s options if prevented from exercising permitted act by TPM

content.p: Nothing in this Act prevents any person from using a TPM circumvention device to exercise a permitted act.

blockList.listIntroduction: The user of a TPM work who wishes to exercise a permitted act but cannot practically do so because of a TPM may do either or both of the following:

item.p: apply to the issuer of the TPM work for assistance enabling the user to exercise the permitted act:

engage a qualified person (see section 226D(3)) to exercise the permitted act on the user’s behalf using a TPM circumvention device, but only if the issuer of the TPM work has refused the user’s request for assistance or has failed to respond to it within a reasonable time.

blockList.listIntroduction: Nothing in this Act prevents any person from using a TPM circumvention device to undertake encryption research if that research is a permitted act and if that person—

item.p: is either—
engaged in a course of study at an educational establishment in the field of encryption technology; or
employed, trained, or experienced in the field of encryption technology; and
has either—
obtained permission from the issuer of the TPM work to use a TPM circumvention device for the purpose of the research; or
has taken, or will take, all reasonable steps to obtain that permission.

content.p: A qualified person who exercises a permitted act on behalf of the user of a TPM work must not charge the user more than a sum consisting of the total of the cost of the provision of the service and a reasonable contribution to the qualified person’s general expenses.

section.heading: Meaning of copyright management information

blockList.listIntroduction: In sections 226G, 226H, and 226J, CMI or copyright management information means information attached to, or appearing in connection with communicating or making available, a copy of a copyright work that—

item.p: identifies 1 or more of the following:
the work:
the author of the work:
the copyright owner:
a performer:
in the case of a film, the director of the film; or
identifies or indicates some or all of the terms and conditions for using the work, or indicates that the use of the work is subject to terms and conditions; or
is a number or code that represents any of the information referred to in paragraph (a) or (b).

section.heading: Interference with CMI prohibited

content.p: A person (A) must not remove or modify any copyright management information attached to, or appearing in connection with communicating or making available, a copy of a work.

blockList.listIntroduction: However, subsection (1) does not apply if—

item.p: A has the authority of the copyright owner or the exclusive licensee to remove or modify the copyright management information; or
A does not know, and has no reason to believe, that the removal or modification will induce, enable, facilitate, or conceal an infringement of the copyright in the work.

section.heading: Commercial dealing in work subject to CMI interference

content.p: A person (A) must not, in the course of business, make, import, sell, let for hire, offer or expose for sale or hire, or advertise for sale or hire, a copy of a work if any copyright management information attached to, or appearing in connection with communicating or making available, the copy has been removed or modified without the authority of the copyright owner or the exclusive licensee.

blockList.listIntroduction: However, subsection (1) does not apply if—

item.p: A has the authority of the copyright owner or the exclusive licensee to remove or modify the copyright management information; or
A does not know, and has no reason to believe, that the removal or modification will induce, enable, facilitate, or conceal an infringement of the copyright in the work; or

A does not know, and has no reason to believe, that any copyright management information attached to, or appearing in connection with communicating or making available, the copy has been removed or modified without the authority of the copyright owner or the exclusive licensee.

section.heading: Contravention of section 226G or 226H

content.p: A copyright owner or licensee of a work has the same rights in relation to a contravention of section 226G or 226H as a copyright owner has in respect of an infringement of copyright.

If the copyright management information is or includes information that identifies an author, a director, or a performer (or is a number or code that represents information that identifies that person), the author, director, or performer (or a person entitled to exercise that person’s rights under Part 4 or 9) has the same rights and remedies in relation to a contravention of either of sections 226G and 226H as an author, a director, or a performer has in respect of an infringement of the rights conferred by Part 4 or 9.
Subsection (2) does not limit subsection (1).

section.heading: Offence of dealing in work subject to CMI interference

blockList.listIntroduction: A person (A) who contravenes section 226H commits an offence if—

item.p: A knows that the copyright management information has been removed or modified without the authority of the copyright owner or exclusive licensee; and
A knows that dealing in the work will induce, enable, facilitate, or conceal an infringement of the copyright in the work.

content.p: A person who commits an offence under subsection (1) is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $150,000 or a term of imprisonment not exceeding 5 years or both.

section.heading: Offence of fraudulently receiving programmes

content.p: Every person commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $5,000 who, with intent to avoid payment of any charge applicable to the reception of a programme included in a communication work provided from a place in New Zealand, receives such a programme.

blockList.listIntroduction: Where any body corporate is convicted of an offence against this section, every director and every person concerned in the management of the body corporate shall be guilty of the offence if it is proved—

item.p: that the act that constituted the offence took place with his or her authority, permission, or consent; and
that he or she—
knew, or could reasonably be expected to have known, that the offence was to be or was being committed; and
failed to take all reasonable steps to prevent or stop it.

section.heading: Rights and remedies in respect of apparatus, etc, for unauthorised reception of transmissions

blockList.listIntroduction: A person who—

item.p: makes charges for the reception of programmes included in a communication work provided from a place in New Zealand; or
sends encrypted transmissions of any other description from a place in New Zealand—

content.p: is entitled to the rights and remedies in subsections (2) and (3).

blockList.listIntroduction: A person to whom subsection (1) applies—

item.p: has the same rights and remedies against a person referred to in subsection (3) as a copyright owner has in respect of an infringement of copyright; and
has the same rights under section 122 or section 132 in relation to any apparatus or device (of the kind referred to in subsection (3)﻿(a)) as a copyright owner has in relation to an infringing copy.

blockList.listIntroduction: The person referred to in subsection (2) is a person who—

item.p: makes, imports, sells, or lets for hire any apparatus or device designed or adapted to enable or assist persons to receive the programmes or other transmissions when they are not entitled to do so; or
publishes any information that is calculated to enable or assist persons to receive the programmes or other transmissions when they are not entitled to do so.

content.p: In section 121(1) as it applies to proceedings for infringement of the rights conferred by this section, the reference to the defendant not knowing or having reason to believe that copyright existed in the work shall be construed as a reference to not knowing or having reason to believe that the acts complained of infringed the rights conferred by this section.
Section 134 applies, with all necessary modifications, in relation to the disposal of anything delivered up under subsection (2)﻿(b).

section.heading: Supplementary provisions as to fraudulent reception

blockList.listIntroduction: The Governor-General may from time to time, by Order in Council,—

item.p: provide that section 227 applies in relation to programmes included in services provided from a country or territory outside New Zealand; and
provide that section 228 applies in relation to such programmes and to encrypted transmissions sent from such a country or territory.

content.p: No such order shall be made unless it appears to the Governor-General that provision has been or will be made under the laws of that country or territory giving adequate protection to persons making charges for programmes included in communication works provided from New Zealand or, as the case may be, for encrypted transmissions sent from New Zealand.

Where sections 227 and 228 apply in relation to a communication work, they also apply to any service run for the person providing that service, or a person providing programmes for that service, where the service so run consists wholly or mainly in the sending by means of a telecommunications system of sounds or visual images, or both.
An order under this section is secondary legislation (see Part 3 of the Legislation Act 2019 for publication requirements).

section.heading: Application to convention countries

blockList.listIntroduction: Subject to subsection (2), the provisions of this Act, other than the provisions of Part 9, shall—

item.p: apply in relation to persons who are citizens or subjects of any convention country or are domiciled or resident there, as they apply in relation to persons who are New Zealand citizens or are domiciled or resident in New Zealand:
apply in relation to bodies incorporated under the law of any convention country as they apply in relation to bodies incorporated under the law of New Zealand:
apply in relation to works first published in any convention country as they apply in relation to works first published in New Zealand:
apply in relation to communication works communicated from any convention country as they apply in relation to communication works communicated from New Zealand,—

content.p: until the close of 31 December 1995 or, in relation to any particular convention country, the coming into force in respect of that convention country of an Order in Council made under section 232, whichever is the earlier.

For the avoidance of doubt, it is hereby declared that subsection (1) applies, in relation to a state of affairs or an action referred to in that subsection as existing or taking place in a convention country, whether or not the country in which the state of affairs existed or the action was taken was, at the time the state of affairs existed or the action was taken, a convention country.

blockList.listIntroduction: No provision of this Act shall apply, pursuant to subsection (1), to a work made before the commencement of this Act unless—

item.p: copyright existed in the work under the Copyright Act 1962 immediately before the commencement of this Act; or
the work enjoyed protection in the nature of copyright in any convention country and, at the commencement of this Act, the term of that protection had not expired; or
the work was first published in a convention country.

section.heading: Expenditure or liability incurred in connection with copyright work

blockList.listIntroduction: This section applies in any case where—

item.p: a work was made before the commencement of this Act; and
copyright did not exist in the work under the Copyright Act 1962 when the work was made; and
on the commencement of this Act, copyright exists in the work pursuant to section 230.

content.p: Where, in any case to which subsection (1) applies, a person incurred any expenditure or liability relating to an act that, at the time the act was done, was not an act restricted by copyright in the work, the person does not do an act restricted by copyright by doing, or continuing to do, that act in respect of the work when copyright exists in the work.

Notwithstanding subsection (2), an act that under that subsection is not an act restricted by copyright when copyright exists in the work may become an act restricted by copyright if the owner of the copyright or his or her exclusive licensee (if any) pays the person such compensation for the person's expenditure or liability as may be agreed upon or, in default of agreement, as shall be determined by arbitration in accordance with the provisions of the Arbitration Act 1908.

section.heading: Application of Act (other than Part 9) to other entities

content.p: On the recommendation of the Minister, the Governor-General may by Order in Council apply any provision or provisions of this Act (other than a provision of Part 9) to any entity specified in the order (whether a State, part of a State, a territory for whose international relations a State is responsible, a political union, an international organisation, or any other entity).

blockList.listIntroduction: To the extent that the nature of the entity permits, an order may apply a provision to an entity so that it has all or any of the following effects:

item.p: it applies to persons who are citizens or subjects of, or domiciled or resident in, the entity as it applies to persons who are citizens or subjects of, or domiciled or resident in, New Zealand:
it applies to bodies incorporated under the law of the entity as it applies to bodies incorporated under the law of New Zealand:
it applies to works first published in the entity as it applies to works first published in New Zealand:
it applies to communication works communicated from any convention country as it applies to communication works communicated from New Zealand.

blockList.listIntroduction: An order—

item.p: may apply a provision unconditionally, or subject to conditions, modifications, or both; and
may apply a provision generally, or in relation to works or cases of a particular class or classes.

blockList.listIntroduction: The Minister must not recommend the making of an order applying any provision of this Act to any entity unless satisfied that—

item.p: the entity is a convention country; or

provision is or will be made under the law of or applicable to the entity giving reciprocal protection to copyright owners in respect of works generally or (as the case requires) works or cases of the class or classes to which the order applies that provision of this Act.

blockList.listIntroduction: If the Government of a State is responsible for the international relations of 1 or more territories, an order may apply a provision to—

item.p: both the State and the territory (or 1 or more of the territories) concerned; or
just the State; or
just the territory (or 1 or more of the territories) concerned.

blockList.listIntroduction: If—

item.p: an unpublished work is of unknown authorship, but there are reasonable grounds to suppose that the author was at the material time a citizen or subject of, or domiciled or resident in, an entity other than New Zealand; and

an order under this section has applied a provision of this Act to that entity so that it applies to persons who are citizens or subjects of the entity, or are domiciled or resident there, as it applies to persons who are citizens or subjects of, or domiciled or resident in, New Zealand; and
a person is authorised under the law of or applicable to the entity to represent the author, or protect and enforce the rights of the author in relation to the work,—

content.p: the authorised person must be treated as if he or she were the author of the work for the purposes of the provision.
An order under this section is secondary legislation (see Part 3 of the Legislation Act 2019 for publication requirements).

section.heading: Denial of copyright to persons connected with countries not giving adequate protection to New Zealand works

content.p: Whenever it appears to the Governor-General that the law of a country, other than a convention country, fails to give adequate protection to copyright in New Zealand works, or to 1 or more classes of such works, the Governor-General may by Order in Council make provision in accordance with this section restricting the rights conferred by this Act in relation to that country.

blockList.listIntroduction: An Order in Council made under this section shall designate the country concerned and provide that, for the purposes specified in the order, works first published after a date specified in the order shall not be treated as qualifying for copyright by virtue of such publication if at that time the authors are—

item.p: citizens or subjects of that country (not domiciled or resident in New Zealand); or
bodies incorporated under the law of that country;—

content.p: and the order may make such provision for all purposes of this Act or for such purposes as are specified in the order, and either generally or in relation to such classes of cases as are specified in the order, having regard to the nature and extent of the failure referred to in subsection (1).

An Order in Council under this section may be so made as to apply generally to a country, or to any territories for whose international relations the Government of that country is responsible, or to the country exclusive of all or any such territories.
In this section,—
An order under this section is secondary legislation (see Part 3 of the Legislation Act 2019 for publication requirements).

prescribing classes of libraries for the purposes of section 50:
prescribing institutions for the purposes of section 117:
prescribing bodies for the purposes of section 72, 89, 90, 185, 190, or 191:
prescribing classes of communication works for the purposes of section 90 or section 191:
prescribing the form of a notice of infringement for the purposes of section 92D:
prescribing the form, content, procedures, requirements, and any other matters relating to infringement notices:
prescribing the form of notice for challenging an infringement notice:
prescribing the fee payable by rights owners for applications to the Tribunal under section 122J:
prescribing the practices and procedures of the Tribunal in relation to determining applications under section 122J:
prescribing the sum, or a method or methods of calculating the sum, that the Tribunal may order an account holder to pay under section 122O:
prescribing any matters necessary or desirable in relation to an order, or an application for an order, under section 122P:
prescribing the rate or rates, or a method or methods for calculating the rate or rates, for the fees that may be charged by IPAPs to rights owners under section 122U:

prescribing the particulars to be contained in a notice given under section 136(1):

requiring a person giving a notice under section 136(1), either at the time of giving the notice or subsequently, to furnish evidence in support of the claim that an item is a work in which the person owns the copyright:

a person giving a notice under section 136(1), either at the time of giving the notice or subsequently; or

forms to be signed by specified persons:

the contents of the constitution or other form of rules of the licensing body or bodies:
the representation of copyright owners in the management of the licensing body or bodies:
the collection, holding, and distribution of money by the licensing body or bodies:
the disclosure of the financial affairs of the licensing body or bodies:
